A.best_element: Solves unattended Calendar auth with no backend: a personal GCP-project setup guide, PKCE plus a stored refresh token, publishing to Production unverified to avoid the 7-day Testing expiry, the calendar.app.created scope, the base32hex event-ID rule (the 'w' in 'sgw' is invalid), and a reconciliation state machine with 409/cancelled handling.
A.biggest_weakness: Heavily lopsided toward Google auth. ShopGoodwill gets one thin paragraph: no Terms of Use quote (the Terms explicitly ban browser extensions), no DOM/SPA re-render guidance, no session-reuse detail (it implies credential login via SignIn/Login), and no prior art or seeded QoL.

B.best_element: Contracts-first Phase 0 that freezes the SgwClient, ListingCardAdapter, Scheduler, CalendarSink, and BidExecutor interfaces before parallel work. Pairs it with honest reliability tiers (T0 extension-only, T1 Chrome background/keep-awake, T2 companion) and endpoints checked against the live bundle (RemoveItemFromFavoriteList, GetCurrentTime, RefreshToken, cookieSession_8).
B.biggest_weakness: Says the Terms of Use stance on automation is 'unverified' when the 2025-01-22 Terms explicitly prohibit any 'browser extension' that extracts data or modifies page rendering. A few platform claims (Chrome 148 native browser.*, polyfill archived Jul 2026) are asserted without verify flags.

C.best_element: Built for isolated agents: tests-first lists and gate commands per task, a ports-and-adapters domain with contracts and example payloads, test-only hooks compiled out with a CI proof, a no-live-writes rule, and fail-closed runtime schema validation. Tooling facts are correct: Playwright loads extensions in Chromium only, MSW cannot intercept inside an extension worker, and unpacked builds bypass the 30 s alarm minimum.
C.biggest_weakness: Marks the ShopGoodwill Terms stance as unknown when the Terms explicitly ban extensions and scripts. Prior art and snipe-timing guidance are thin. Saying Firefox MV3 host permissions are opt-in is dated: Firefox 127+ grants them at install, though users can still revoke them.

E.best_element: The richest prior-art and UX grounding: MarketClean, Crumb, failure modes of low-rated hiders, the storage.sync quota trap, and Gixen snipe groups. It requires hiding never be silent (a 'Why?' per card, one-click undo, an 'SGW layout changed' degraded state) and flags that auto-favoriting may attract rival bidders.
E.biggest_weakness: States unverified claims as fact: 'there is no clock extension', the 30-day/15-auction cap, 6-8 PM Pacific peaks, notes up to 500 characters (the community client truncates at 256), and 403s caused by request bursts. It gives no guidance on the SGW session or token, and the UX-spec deliverable (wireframes, microcopy) will bloat the plan.

F.best_element: The most rigorous money-safety design. Terms quoted and treated as first-class, with a user go/no-go before any bidding code. The snipe submits the single proxy max once. Total open-exposure cap, auto-kill on anomalies, a T-60s re-check, retry only when the bid provably never arrived, and an outcome taxonomy. The mock buyerapi injects skew, latency, and soft-close extension.
F.biggest_weakness: Weighted toward the nice-to-have sniper: hide/highlight, daily checks, favoriting, and Calendar get almost no guidance (no SPA re-render or DOM notes). It asks for Playwright extension E2E on both browsers, but Firefox is unsupported. It marks GetCurrentTime and serverTime as unverified, though both exist.

rationale: C's prompt makes Fable write a plan that matches how this team will execute: every task carries tests-first lists, gate commands, owned files and example-payload contracts, and the safety controls are themselves tested (hooks compiled out, no live writes, fail-closed schemas). Its tooling facts are also the most correct for cross-browser E2E. B is close: it has broader platform facts and a good contracts-first Phase 0, but weaker test and safety rigor. Both miss that the ShopGoodwill Terms explicitly ban extensions.
